findings.criterion: 1 — resident can generate and share a usable, tamper-protected 2-hour pass
findings.issue: The new joined test starts from a fabricated token, mounts GuestPass directly, and mocks both lookup and redemption as successful. It therefore does not execute resident generation/share, the real /pass route under AppProvider, or server HMAC/verify-code/expiry validation for the displayed artifact.
findings.consequence: The tests still do not establish that the artifact a resident actually shares survives unauthenticated app bootstrap and is accepted by the real gate endpoints as the same live pass.
findings.correction: Issue a live pass through the API, invoke the resident share control, open its fragment URL through the real /pass route at a mobile viewport, decode the rendered QR, and perform real lookup/redeem; assert the token identity, 2-hour expiry, and tamper rejection.

findings.criterion: 2 plus accessibility — rejected scanned passes remain safely and accessibly surfaced after camera navigation
findings.issue: The routed test covers only success. The delayed rejection-after-camera-navigation case remains a pure state harness, and the real Confirm rejection banner has neither tabIndex/ref nor an effect that moves focus; focus handling exists only in CheckInCapture.
findings.consequence: When the camera navigates while lookup is pending and the pass then rejects, the guard blocks submission but keyboard users lose focus when the camera control unmounts and are not moved to the required acknowledgment.
findings.correction: Make the Confirm rejection banner programmatically focusable and focus it when passError appears, then add a routed deferred-lookup test that triggers camera navigation, rejects on Confirm, asserts alert focus and disabled/no walk-in submission, and acknowledges back to capture.

findings.criterion: 3 and 4 — camera plate scanning during check-in and check-out
findings.issue: The new tests replace LiveCamera with a button and never execute getUserMedia, the ONNX/model decoder, a camera fixture, or a responsive browser. They prove only the already-visible onPlate callback wiring; the existing check-in browser story remains unrecorded and checkout still has no camera browser story.
findings.consequence: Whether an attendant can actually acquire and decode a plate through the shipped camera stack on check-in or checkout remains unverified.
findings.correction: Run and record the 390x844 fake-camera check-in story with its model/fixture, add and run the equivalent checkout story, and assert the visible plate, match request/result, browser/model/fixture versions, and clean console.

findings.criterion: 6 and 7 — complete Admin CRUD and Super Admin cross-property operations
findings.issue: The new test executes CRUD only for units. People is mounted only to change a property selector and assert a platform-scoped units read; it performs no person mutation, never mounts the site/slot CRUD screen, performs no mutation in the second property, and has no narrow-viewport or server-denial execution for a regular admin.
findings.consequence: Person/site/slot UI CRUD, mobile usability, Super Admin writes across properties, and the regular-admin property boundary are still not established in context.
findings.correction: Drive create/edit/delete for person, site, unit, and slot through the real screens at a narrow viewport; switch a Super Admin to a second property and perform representative writes there; execute regular-admin cross-property read/write denials against the API.

findings.criterion: cross-cutting security/data integrity — idempotency on writes
findings.issue: HTTP replay protection runs only when a route declares idempotent, but the required unit/person/site/slot creation routes do not. The client sends a key that these routes ignore. A committed local-auth person creation whose response is lost creates the account and one-time password; retry then reaches already_member instead of replaying a recoverable result.
findings.consequence: Network or intermediary retries can surface false failures and, for person creation, strand onboarding after the only temporary password response is lost; duplicate audit/side effects are also not replay-safe.
findings.correction: Make the CRUD mutations replay-safe with server-enforced idempotency and client-stable submission keys. For local-user creation, use an invitation/password-setup or explicit recovery result rather than depending on replaying a redacted one-time secret. Add same-key replay tests proving one entity/audit mutation and a usable retry outcome.
